extracted.intended_audience: literate public, theatre patrons, writers and critics interested in literary taste and dramatic representation (early-18th-century readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Short essays and commentary offering evaluative guidance on translation choices, dramatic and poetic representation, acting quality, and the moral/political effects of theatre and rhetoric. Focuses on what makes characters, performances, and works effective or appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose epithets consistent with character to avoid burlesque
rubrics_metrics.description: the poet has therefore wisely dropped them both for Dux Trojanus ... for he very well knew a loose action might be consistent enough with the usual manners of a soldier, though it became neither the chastity of a pious man, nor the gravity of the father of a people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When translating or applying epithets, select terms that suit the character's established persona and social role; avoid phrases that create an unintended burlesque or undermine dignity. Example: prefer 'Dux Trojanus' to contradictory epithets like 'Pius Æneas' when the depicted action clashes with the virtue implied by the epithet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain internal consistency of character behaviour and virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: a loose action might be consistent enough with the usual manners of a soldier, though it became neither the chastity of a pious man, nor the gravity of the father of a people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that actions ascribed to a character align with the virtues or roles previously established; when they diverge, provide justification or risk undermining credibility and moral tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer presentation of noble characters to elevate public taste
rubrics_metrics.description: The amendment of these low gratifications is only to be made by people of condition, by encouraging the presentation of the noble characters drawn by Shakespeare and others, from whence it is impossible to return without strong impressions of honour and humanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers, patrons, and the upper classes should encourage dramas that portray noble, honourable characters so theatre cultivates polite and moral behaviour in society rather than pandering to low gratifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatic representation must use person, manner, look, and motion
rubrics_metrics.description: when the character he draws is presented by the person, the manner, the look, and the motion, of an accomplished player?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An actor's full embodiment—physical presence, gestures, facial expression, and movement—is essential to convey a character convincingly; excellence in these elements multiplies the power of the written role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation (painting/history/poetry/theatre) should create vivid impressions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a thing painted or related can irresistibly enter our hearts, what may not be performed by an excellent poet... You have in that one sentence, a lively impression of his whole life and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artistic accounts (visual or verbal) should aim to produce a single, vivid impression that conveys character and life; use concentrated, telling detail (as in Le Brun's painting or Sallust's account of Catiline) to move the audience to pity, horror, or admiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theatre is an effective tool for moral and polite education
rubrics_metrics.description: Eugenio ended his discourse, by recommending the apt use of a theatre, as the most agreeable and easy method of making a polite and moral gentry, which would end in rendering the rest of the people regular in their behaviour, and ambitious of laudable undertakings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staging virtuous, high-minded drama can cultivate manners and public morals; theatre producers and patrons should recognize and use the stage's pedagogic potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actors perform best when matched with equally excellent partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Skilful actors think it a very peculiar happiness to play in a scene with such as top their parts... those excellent players seem to be in their most shining circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casting should consider ensemble dynamics: pairing strong performers together elevates each actor's performance and the scene's overall effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic acting requires naturalness and propriety in portraying folly
rubrics_metrics.description: he has a peculiar talent of looking like a fool, and therefore excellently well qualified for the part of Biskett... that with such a natural air and propriety of folly...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful comic performance depends on a natural, credible portrayal of folly rather than exaggerated or mechanical clowning; propriety and an appearance of effortless absurdity are virtues for comic actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low or 'low-life' comedy should be just and witty in representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole comedy is very just, and the low part of human life represented with much humour and wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When depicting base or low characters and situations, the play should treat them with accuracy and cleverness—truthful representation and wit preserve artistic value rather than descending into mere vulgarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective leadership rhetoric should persuade by reason and praise, not risky bravado
rubrics_metrics.description: Cæsar would not leave the success of his speech to such uncertain events: he shows his men the unreasonableness of their fears in an obliging manner, and concludes, that if none else would march along with them, he would go himself with the Tenth Legion... The Tenth Legion, fired with the praises of their general, send thanks to him ... and the rest, ashamed to be outdone, assure him, that they are as ready to follow where he pleases to lead them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rhetoric aimed at motivating followers should expose the irrationality of fears gently, single out and praise reliable subgroups, and offer a measured personal commitment—this wins loyalty more safely than theatrical threats or extreme displays that depend on uncertain audience reaction.
